examples.visibleExplanation: A non-East player wins with East's first discard.
examples.accessibleDescription: Earth's Blessing event sequence: East makes the first discard of the hand, another player claims it, and that discard completes Mahjong.

examples.accessibleDescription: current rules Buzzard All Winds and Dragons example: Pungs of East, South, West and North Winds, plus a pair of Red Dragons.

examples.accessibleDescription: current rules Buzzard Three Winds and a Pair example: Pungs of East, South and West Winds, a pair of North Winds, and a Pung of 5 Circles. Buzzard source evidence also permits a non-winning limit case not represented by this example.

examples.accessibleDescription: current rules Buzzard All Ones and Nines example: Pungs of 1 Bamboo, 9 Circles, 1 Character and 9 Bamboo, plus a pair of 9 Characters.

entries.summary: Four concealed Pungs and a concealed pair in one suit. The winning rules depend on the version you play.
entries.whatItIs: Make four concealed Pungs and a concealed pair in one numbered suit.
entries.whatItMeans: Keep the hand concealed. The rules also set how you must win.
entries.whySpecial: The concealed Pungs and the way you win make this hand unusual.

entries.summary: A non-East player wins from East’s first discard.
entries.whatItMeans: The hand shape can be ordinary; the special comes from the exact moment and discarder that provide the winning tile.
entries.whySpecial: East’s first discard ends the hand before normal play develops.
entries.referenceNote: This BMJA hand is won from East’s first discard.

entries.displayName: Gathering the Plum Blossom from the Roof
entries.summary: A replacement draw gives you the 5 Circles that completes Mahjong.
entries.whatItIs: Draw the 5 Circles as a replacement tile, and use it to win.
entries.whatItMeans: The final hand shape alone is not enough; the scorer needs to know that 5 Circles arrived as the qualifying replacement draw.
entries.whySpecial: The winning tile must be the 5 Circles drawn as a replacement tile.

evidenceBindings.locator: Event-dependent specials — Gathering the Plum Blossom from the Roof

entries.displayName: Plucking the Moon from the Bottom of the Sea
entries.summary: The last drawable tile is 1 Circle, and it completes Mahjong.
entries.whatItIs: Draw the last live-wall tile, the 1 Circle, and use it to win.
entries.whatItMeans: The winning tile and its place in the wall both matter. The same final tiles won another way do not make this hand.
entries.whySpecial: The hand must win on the 1 Circle from the last live-wall draw.

evidenceBindings.locator: Event-dependent specials — Plucking the Moon from the Bottom of the Sea

entries.summary: Four Pungs or Kongs and a pair made only from Winds and Dragons.
entries.whatItIs: Make four honour Pungs or Kongs and a pair. Buzzard scores this named hand at the table limit.
entries.whatItMeans: Every set and the pair are Winds or Dragons. No suited tiles appear.
entries.whySpecial: Buzzard lists All Winds and Dragons among its ten limit hands, irrespective of ordinary score value.
entries.referenceNote: This describes the Buzzard 2000 hand. Other rules may define a hand with the same name differently.

evidenceBindings.locator: §B Winner only — All Winds and Dragons; §D Limit hands item 1

entries.summary: Three Wind Pungs or Kongs, a pair of the fourth Wind, and one more set.
entries.whatItIs: A Buzzard hand with Pungs or Kongs of three Winds and a pair of the fourth Wind.
entries.whatItMeans: The winning form has Pung/Kongs of three distinct Winds, a pair of the fourth Wind, and one ordinary Chow, Pung or Kong. It is materially different from Four Blessings, which requires four Wind Pung/Kongs.
entries.whySpecial: Buzzard requires three Wind sets, the fourth Wind as a pair, and one other set.
entries.referenceNote: Buzzard also has a separate table-score rule for some hands that do not win as this special hand.

evidenceBindings.locator: §D Limit hands / retained PDF p.11 — completed Four-Wind hand

entries.summary: Mahjong is made with East Wind's first discard.
entries.whatItIs: A special win from East’s first discard. Buzzard scores it at the table limit.
entries.whatItMeans: The completed hand does not define the special by itself; the winning tile must be East's first discard.
entries.whySpecial: Buzzard lists this immediate first-discard win among its ten limit hands.
entries.referenceNote: This describes the Buzzard 2000 rule. It does not establish that every ruleset uses the same rule as BMJA Earth’s Blessing.

entries.summary: Four Pungs or Kongs and a pair made only from suited 1s and 9s.
entries.whatItIs: Use only the 1 and 9 tiles from Bamboo, Circles and Characters.
entries.whatItMeans: Winds and Dragons are not part of this hand.
entries.whySpecial: Buzzard lists All Ones and Nines among its ten limit hands.
entries.referenceNote: Buzzard scores this hand at the table limit. Other rules may score similar tile patterns differently.

evidenceBindings.locator: heads-and-tails / local name All Ones and Nines

entries.summary: Four concealed Pungs or Kongs and a pair.
entries.whatItIs: Make four concealed Pungs or Kongs and a pair. Buzzard scores this named hand at the table limit.
entries.whatItMeans: The grouped structure is ordinary, but every meld must satisfy the concealed Pung/Kong condition represented by the current detector.
entries.whySpecial: Buzzard scores concealed Pungs and Kongs as a named limit hand.

evidenceBindings.locator: §D Limit hands item 7; §B remove generic fully-concealed ordinary double

entries.summary: East wins a thirteenth consecutive hand while remaining East.
entries.whatItIs: East wins the thirteenth hand in a row.
entries.whatItMeans: This depends on the game history, not on a particular tile pattern.
entries.whySpecial: Buzzard rewards the thirteenth consecutive East win as a limit event.
